title: Current Position | Weekly Briefing November 18th to November 24th [PODCAST]
summary: Stay updated on critical supply chain shifts, including new customs rules and market trends, to navigate global trade effectively.
body_markdown:
Regulatory changes, shifting capacity, and operational disruptions continue to reshape how goods move across global supply chains. From new customs requirements and evolving trade rules to changing air and ocean capacity and potential ground transportation disruptions, staying informed, planning ahead, and building flexibility into supply chain strategies remain critical for navigating what comes next.


• 6 min


Current Position | Weekly Briefing November 18th - 24th


The Expeditors Podcast


Play


**


You're listening to Current Position, a weekly briefing from Expeditors mapping the shifts across trade compliance, regulatory changes, and global supply chains. Plus, no market insights this week - I'm all by my lonesome!


I'm Chris Parker, and here's the latest from November 18th to November 24th.


**Global Customs & Trade Market**


-


U.S. importers have just over a month to verify their U.S. company status with their customs brokers. U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) issued an interim final rule (IFR) earlier this month establishing new requirements for companies importing goods into the US, and new responsibilities for licensed customs brokers to validate US Importer of Record. Importers must be ready, before Jan. 5, to provide documentation brokers need to confirm their company's qualification as a U.S. Importer of Record. Not being prepared to provide the necessary documentation could lead to delays or interruptions to customs clearance in the new year.


[Read more](https://nam12.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Finfo.expeditors.com%2Fnewsflash%2Fcbp-issues-interim-final-rule-on-new-requirements-for-foreign-iors&data=05%7C02%7CSamantha.Hurst%40expeditors.com%7Cd748595a54f246a369e408df4a57654e%7Cfe7654e8131d4caabe5c31e128506c40%7C0%7C0%7C639311411347161024%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=PdOXV20yEY5xh7y1DOCOE%2BXtNDbajGGJqkWnMye80ZU%3D&reserved=0) .


-


UK importers should prepare for new import requirements related to steel in Q2 of 2027. Beginning in April 2027, importers may voluntarily report through the Customs Declaration Service the country where imported steel was first melted and poured. The reporting will become mandatory in July of next year. Importers must provide evidence such as a Mill Test Certificate showing the country of origin.


[Read more](https://info.expeditors.com/newsflash/uk-introduces-melt-and-pour-reporting-requirements-for-steel-imports?hsLang=en-us) .


-


The UK and EU have agreed to scrap most food and plant health checks and certificates from 1 March 2028. Negotiations concluded at the Brussels summit, with the SPS agreement eliminating a requirement for certificates and controls on most food, plants and animals moving between Great Britain and the EU. The change has received mixed reviews from the UK and EU transportation community.


[Read more](https://trans.info/en/uk-eu-deal-sps-2028-hgv-drivers-90-180-rule-516053) .


Global Ocean Market


-


The Pacific Maritime Association (PMA) and ILWU Local 26 reached a tentative agreement over the weekend to prevent a strike of 250 watchmen at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach. The deal allowed for the current contract to be extended and a strike to be avoided while a vote is finalized by the Local 26 members. While Local 26 covers a small percentage of security guard workers at the two ports, there was concern that all port workers would honor the strike.[Read more](https://maritime-executive.com/article/ports-of-la-and-long-beach-avert-strike-as-watchmen-reach-deal) .


-


Far East to Mediterranean spot rates jumped 6.8% as the return to the Red Sea stalled. Xeneta says the Mediterranean rate reached USD 4,989 per FEU, USD 1,551 above North Europe, which fell 2.3% to USD 3,438. Bab el-Mandeb container transits fell from a seven-day average of 16.6 a day on 25 October to 11.9 on 19 November. Chief Analyst Peter Sand expects rates to trend downward into 2027, but the fragile Red Sea situation makes unexpected spikes likely.[Read more](https://www.ajot.com/news/xeneta-weekly-ocean-container-shipping-market-update-november-20-2026) .


Global Air Market


-


Air cargo rates rose for a seventh straight week in week 46 as capacity in the market continued to shrink. WorldACD data shows the global average rate rose 2%, from $3.04 in mid-September to $3.49 per kg. This rate is 32% above a year earlier, while capacity fell 2% and volume fell 4%. Several factors contributed to the fluctuation, including the Diwali holiday in South Asia and the US air traffic control outage. Asia Pacific to Europe traffic was down 15% year on year, a seventh consecutive week of double-digit decline.


[Read more](https://www.ajot.com/news/weekly-air-cargo-trends-november-9-to-15-2026) .


-


Europe's e-commerce changes earlier this year continue to cause freighter operators to shift capacity from the Asia-Europe trade to the transpacific. E-commerce imports into Europe were down on average 44% over the last three months compared to June, according to e-commerce consultant Rotate, this decline caused a subsequent 46% drop in outbound freighter capacity from China and Hong Kong versus June.


[Read more](https://www.aircargonews.net/editorial/2026/11/freighters-shift-to-the-transpacific-as-asia-europe-e-commerce-falls/) .


Global Ground Transport Market


-


French border control staff may strike at Boulogne and Dunkirk between 21 November and 31 December. The UK's Animal and Plant Health Agency warned that staff at the Boulogne and Dunkirk posts may strike on selected dates, with the first disruption expected on Saturday 21 November, after strike action already hit Calais on 18 November. Consignments needing sanitary or phytosanitary inspection are most at risk. SIVEP will maintain minimum staffing and may redirect some UK consignments, but queues remain possible as pre-Christmas traffic builds.


[Read more](https://trans.info/en/french-border-strikes-could-disrupt-uk-eu-freight-from-21-november-515393) .


-


Mexican truckers have secured a win for highway safety with the country's government after conducting nationwide strikes last month. A total of 29 agreements aim to address issues such as deteriorating infrastructure, highway security, and cargo theft. These agreements follow on the heels of trucker protests that disrupted freight transportation across 19 states over the course of a month.


[Read more](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/borderlands-mexico-truckers-secure-29-agreements-on-highway-safety-after-nationwide-strike) .


-


The European Commission plans to withdraw its late-payment proposal that would have put measures in place to prevent carriers from having to wait up to 120 days to be paid. Proposed regulation called for payment terms of no more than 30 days in most commercial transactions. A pending withdrawal of the proposal is possible as a council reviewing the proposal remained in deadlock over the topic. Spain, which has put its own penalties in place, saw its average payment wait fall to a record 47 days in September 2026.


[Read more](https://trans.info/en/a-120-day-payment-period-for-freight-charges-is-still-the-norm-meanwhile-the-european-commission-wants-to-withdraw-a-proposal-to-curb-payment-backlogs-515420) .


You are now at our current position. Links to everything we covered today, plus some extra articles of interest, are in the show notes.


And while you're there, check out the events and webinars we flagged for the weeks ahead. Thank you for listening, and we'll see you next week.
